chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Sulayman ibn Ja'far al-Ja'fari, who said:
I saw Aba al-Hasan al-Rida عليه السلام praying in a khazz cloak.

As for what Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Dawud al-Sarmi, who said: I asked him about salat (prayer) in khazz that is adulterated with rabbit fur, and he wrote: "That is permissible."

This is an anomalous hadith; no one narrated it except Dawud al-Sarmi. Along with his being alone in narrating it, its wordings differ, because in this narration he said, "I asked him," thus attributing the question to himself, yet he did not clarify who the one asked was; and it is possible that the one asked was someone whose statement is not binding to follow.

Then he said in the narration that he mentioned: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad and 'Abd Allah, the two sons of Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Dawud al-Sarmi, who said: A man asked Aba al-Hasan the Third عليه السلام about salat (prayer) in khazz that is adulterated with rabbit fur, and he wrote: "That is permissible."

So he mentioned, as you see in this narration, that the questioner was someone other than himself, and he named the one asked. This is an apparent contradiction, because if the questioner were himself, then the latter narration would necessarily be false; and if the questioner were someone else, then the first would necessarily be false. When two narrations oppose one another and there is nothing to support either of them, both must be set aside. Moreover, even if this hadith were authentic, it would not oppose what we have mentioned of the hadiths; and it is possible that this report was issued in the context of taqiyyah, just as many reports of this kind have been issued.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Salat (prayer) in black garments is disliked, and the turban is not counted among garments in this respect, so there is no problem in praying in it even if it is black.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation for protection, a possible context for a report
key_terms.الثِّيَابِ السُّودِ: black garments, regarding which prayer is said to be disliked
key_terms.الْخَزِّ: khazz, a type of garment material discussed in relation to prayer
key_terms.الْعِمَامَةُ: the turban, excluded here from the disliked ruling on black clothing
key_terms.اَلصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act whose validity is under discussion
key_terms.حَدِيثٌ شَاذٌّ: an anomalous hadith not supported by broader transmission
key_terms.وَبَرِ الْأَرَانِبِ: rabbit fur used as admixture in the garment

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to perform salat (prayer) in khazz clothing mixed with rabbit fur or in black garments?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal ruling on praying in khazz garments, especially those mixed with rabbit fur, and examines conflicting narrations on the issue. It also reflects hadith criticism by identifying anomaly and contradiction in transmission, while concluding with the ruling that prayer in black clothing is disliked, except for the turban.
